rule: Table 2 HGB error gate at every checkpoint
threshold: Original select_threshold: at least five releases and 20% development coverage; largest development coverage with error <= 1 - target. Target .85 reproduces Table 2 HGB exactly.
capability: 5=current5; 10=current10 except when current10 fails the original development HGB gate and5 passes, then use5; 15=current15 for EVERY record. No labels determine this choice. At5 and15 rank current HGB scores. At10 use development-fitted monotone isotonic calibration of the chosen source-time score to compare retained5/current10. Stable record-ID tie break. Fixed predicted candidate for all four panels.
denominator: Coverage: all record-seed events. Agreement: released reports. FNR/FPR: released abnormal/normal reference events. Low/high states: MA <50 / >70 mm.
paper: Original 60 development / 201 evaluation records; 20 development partitions.
internal: Separate frozen 301-record grouped five-fold evaluation; one existing inner-partition setting. Do not pool with the paper cohort or the older three-repeat analysis.
uncertainty: Exploratory alignment after prior inspection. No independent validation or monotonic observed performance guarantee.

prior_control_protocol.capability: Retain the existing increasing isotonic development score-to-error calibration for cross-time comparison, now using HGB scores at every checkpoint. For each record choose the available prediction with the lowest calibrated score. A 1e-6 training percentile breaks plateaus; equal scores retain the earlier prediction. Select floor(quota*N) by score then record identifier, as in Fig. 3. Records can be reselected.
prior_control_protocol.cumulative: Apply the original HGB threshold selector to raw HGB scores separately at each checkpoint, then lock the first accepted prediction. No consensus restriction, boundary gate or test-label decision. Isotonic calibration is used only to compare prediction options in the fixed-coverage panels.

agreement_matching: For each time build the pooled curve from k=1..201 equal-count-per-partition prefixes. For each observed agreement85/90/95%, take the largest attainable coverage and interpolate between adjacent rank-prefix count vectors. Agreement is matched exactly in interpolated aggregate counts. FNR is interpolated FN divided by interpolated released-abnormal count. Identical operating point for b/d.
figure4_protocol: paper dual source only; internal301 remains a separate supplementary evaluation
